slides: Let's continue with more circle tools.

slides.say: The second tool is a ring. Two circles with the same center, O, and the ring between them. Circles with the same center are called concentric. Call the big radius big R, and the small radius r. The ring is the big circle minus the small circle, pi big R squared minus pi r squared.
at: Two circles with the same center
The ring is the big circle

slides.say: Now a chord A B of the big circle that just touches the small circle, at the point M. M is a point of tangency, so the automatic helper line is the radius O M. It's perpendicular to the chord.

Draw O A and O B too. They're radii of the big circle, so triangle A O B is isosceles. O M is the height to its base, and in an isosceles triangle that height is also a median. So M cuts the chord in half. Call each half h.
at: Draw O A and O B
So M cuts the chord in half

slides.say: Look at the right triangle O M B. Its legs are r and h, and its hypotenuse is big R. By Pythagoras, r squared plus h squared is big R squared. Now subtract r squared from both sides. So big R squared minus r squared is h squared.
at: Now subtract r squared from both sides

slides.say: Now return to the whole ring. Its area is pi big R squared minus pi r squared. Take pi as a common factor: pi times the whole bracket, big R squared minus r squared. We just found that the difference inside is h squared. So the ring's area is pi h squared. We need only half the chord, h, not either radius.
at: Now return to the whole ring
Take pi as a common factor

slides.say: So if the chord is ten, then h is half of it, five. And the ring is pi times five squared, twenty-five pi. We don't need either radius.
at: So if the chord is ten
And the ring is pi times

slides.say: Let's check it on rings with a chord of ten. Radii twelve and thirteen, the five, twelve, thirteen triangle. The big circle is pi times thirteen squared, a hundred sixty-nine pi. The small one is pi times twelve squared, a hundred forty-four pi.
The ring is the big circle minus the small one. A hundred sixty-nine pi minus a hundred forty-four pi is twenty-five pi, just like the rule says.
Radii five and five root two, a silver triangle with legs five and five. Five root two, squared, is fifty. Fifty pi minus twenty-five pi is twenty-five pi again.
at: Radii five and five root two

slides.say: And here's the limiting picture, where the small circle has shrunk to a single point, the center. Then the chord goes through the center, so it's a diameter of ten. The ring becomes a whole circle with radius five, twenty-five pi. The same answer.

So when two circles have the same center, and a chord of the big circle touches the small circle, we find the ring's area like this. Take half the chord, square that length, then multiply by pi. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
